correctness.rationale: For the twelve sites, independent exact row reduction gives measurement rank 12; the displayed four independent Hermitian directions are annihilated and so span the kernel. The ideal of the real and imaginary parts of all sixteen cubic minors contains t^5, 4w^3+wt^2, 3x^3+12xt^2+85wt^2, and 81y^3-1237yt^2-306t^3. Exact rational Groebner reductions computed by the standalone checker verify these memberships. The four consequences force all kernel coordinates zero whenever rank is at most two, establishing phase retrieval for every cubic. The twelve-site ambiguity for the smaller radius follows by exact substitution of two explicitly different polynomials; all sub-5 squared radii 1,2,4 are enumerated. No finite experiment is used as a universal proof.

value.rationale: This supplies a concrete twelve-measurement universal phase-retrieval design with small Gaussian-integer coordinates, organized into three fourfold rotational orbits. Such orbits permit four-point angular Fourier reduction and are natural finite polynomial sampling grids. The exact radius-optimality obstruction within the same discrete geometric class distinguishes the instance from a randomly chosen numerical frame and identifies the first feasible lattice footprint. It gives a reusable rank-ideal certificate for a structured dimension-four phase-retrieval construction, not merely a recomputation of a known table.
